items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: we made a recording with Benny Goodman, Billie Holiday, Teddy Wilson

ctx.x: Now who was in this? This was a band that Basie had gotten from Bennie Moten and from Walter Page, and Walter Page came to get you, is that right?
Walter asked me to go to play with him. Of course Mac Washinton was going to play with Benny at the Harlem Club on 15th-La Salle. Ben Webster, Walter Page, and Joe Keyes had me -
Joe Keyes was a great trumpet player.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Shoeless Joe Jackson, that's what they called him... Benny Goodman.

ctx.x: You made this recording for John Hammond produced this? Producers?

I'm pretty sure Brunswick. It was Billie Holiday recording date with Benny Goodman, Walter Page, Buck Clayton, Freddie Green , Mr. Teddy Wilson, and myself. That's all that was on that, and Shoeless Joe Jackson, that's what they called him... Benny Goodman.
You don't remember one name of one of the tunes, do you?

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: They didn't go along with the jazz. ... so far as the Benny Goodmans and the Chick Webbs and the Jimmy Luncefords and what have you.

ctx.x: She joined us - we came into New York in '36, when Billie Holiday joined us in 1937. She stayed with us nearly a year. Things were going and we finally got so that we could leave the Palace Theatre to go to the Apollo Loews State. Naturally when you leave the Loews State you can go from the Loews State to the other theatre and then finally when you was the epitome was when you could play the Paramount, because it was an outmoded thing that

you were going to play the Palace, because the Palace had always established itself in another vein and they did not go with the status quo so far as the Benny Goodmans and the Chick Webbs and the Jimmy Luncefords and what have you. They didn't go along with the jazz.
Was Miss Billie Holiday the first vocalist you had with the band?
